([[Westchester, Florida]]) | college = [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]] (2024–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 25 | draft_team = [[Orlando Magic]] | career_start = 2025 | years1 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team1 = [[Orlando Magic]] | years2 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]] | team2 = →[[Osceola Magic]] | highlights = * Third-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] ([[2024–25 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2025]]) * Big Ten All-Freshman Team (2025) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2024) }} '''Jason Anthoney Richardson II''' (born October 16, 2005) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Orlando Magic]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State Spartans]]. ==Early life and high school career== Richardson was born in [[Berkeley, California]] and grew up in [[Denver]], Colorado.{{cite web|url=https://www.lansingstatejournal.com/story/sports/columnists/graham-couch/2023/10/18/michigan-state-basketball-recruiting-jase-richardson-follow-dad-jason/71226108007/|title=Couch: Jase Richardson is following his dad to MSU, but his mom shaped his game|first=Graham|last=Couch|work=[[Lansing State Journal]]|date=October 18, 2023|access-date=November 5, 2024}} Before the start of his freshman year of high school his family moved to [[Las Vegas]], Nevada where he attended [[Bishop Gorman High School]]. Richardson averaged 14 points, five rebounds, five assists and two steals per game as a sophomore. After missing most of his junior year, Richardson finished his Nike [[EYBL]] career as the third-leading scorer (20.1 PPG) and an unprecedented 10-to-1 assist-to-turnover ratio making him most efficient [[point guard]] regardless of circuit and earning first team Peach Jam Honors.{{cite web|url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2023/jun/01/get-to-know-24-target-jase-richardson/|title=Get to know: '24 target Jase Richardson|first=Richard|last=Davenport|work=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]|date=June 1, 2023|access-date=November 5, 2024}} Richardson transferred to [[Christopher Columbus High School (Miami-Dade County, Florida)|Christopher Columbus High School]] in [[Westchester, Florida]] before the start of his senior season where he averaged 15 points, six rebounds and four assists helping lead Christopher Columbus to their third straight FHSAA 7A State Championship and a final four appearance at Chipotle Nationals alongside [[Cameron Boozer]].{{cite web|url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/high-school/article282234138.html|title=Boozer-Richardson combo propels Columbus to season-opening win over California powerhouse|first=Andre|last=Fernandez|work=[[Miami Herald]]|date=November 22, 2023|access-date=November 5, 2024}} He was rated a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to playing [[college basketball]] for [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]], where his father played, over offers from [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] and [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]].{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |last2=Biancardi |first2=Paul |author-link2=Paul Biancardi |name-list-style=and |date=October 15, 2023 |title=Jase Richardson, son of Jason, commits to Michigan State |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/38667352 |access-date=November 5, 2024 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4964131/2023/10/15/jase-richardson-michigan-state-college-announcement/|title=Michigan State lands 4-star guard Jase Richardson for 2024: What he means for Spartans|first=Tobias|last=Bass|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=October 15, 2023|access-date=November 5, 2024}} ==College career== Richardson enrolled at [[Michigan State University]] in June 2024 in order to take part in the [[2024–25 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Spartans]]' summer practices.{{cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/spartans/2024/07/jase-richardson-making-his-own-way-as-he-joins-michigan-state-roster.html|title=Jase Richardson making his own way as he joins Michigan State roster|first=Kyle|last=Austin|website=[[MLive.com]]|date=July 3, 2024|access-date=November 5, 2024}} He made his college basketball debut during Michigan State's season-opener against [[2024–25 Monmouth Hawks men's basketball team|Monmouth]] on November 4, 2024, and registered 10 points with two rebounds and four assists in an 81–57 win.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/michiganstate/basketball/watch-michigan-state-g-jase-richardson-speaks-on-spartan-debut-01jbxn7npvwm|title=Michigan State G Jase Richardson Speaks on Spartan Debut|first=Aidan|last=Champion|website=[[SI.com]]|date=November 5, 2024|access-date=November 7, 2024}} Richardson came off the bench for most to the season before earning his first career start on February 8, 2025 against [[2024–25 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]],{{Cite web |title=Oregon Ducks vs. Michigan St. Spartans Live Score and Stats - February 8, 2025 Gametracker |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/gametracker/recap/NCAAB_20250208_OREG@MICHST/ |access-date=July 8, 2025 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}} in which he scored a career-high 29 points in the win over the Ducks.{{Cite web |title=Michigan State 86-74 Oregon (Feb 8, 2025) Game Recap |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401721413 |access-date=July 8, 2025 |website=ESPN |language=en}} Richardson started for the remainder of the season and led the Spartans to the Big Ten conference regular-season championship and an Elite Eight appearance in the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where he was selected to the 2025 South Regional Team.{{Cite web |last=Kadlick |first=Mike |date=March 28, 2025 |title=Tom Izzo Sheds Tears As Michigan State Advances to Elite Eight for First Time Since 2019 |url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/tom-izzo-sheds-tears-michigan-state-advances-elite-eight-first-time-since-2019 |access-date=July 8, 2025 |website=SI.com |language=en-US}} Richardson was named to the Big Ten All-Freshman team and [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] third team.{{Cite web |last=Linsner |first=Cory |date=March 11, 2025 |title=Jase Richardson honored on the Big Ten All-Freshman team |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/jase-richardson-honored-big-ten-161818038.html |access-date=July 8, 2025 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}} Richardson announced the end of his college career on April 8, 2025, when he officially made his declaration for the [[2025 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{Cite web |last=Pfeiffer |first=PJ |date=April 8, 2025 |title=Jase Richardson declares for 2025 NBA Draft |url=https://statenews.com/article/2025/04/jase-richardson-declares-for-2025-nba-draft |access-date=July 8, 2025 |website=The State News |language=en-US}} ==Professional career== ===Orlando Magic (2025-present)=== Richardson was selected with the 25th overall pick by the [[Orlando Magic]] in the [[2025 NBA draft]].{{Cite news |last=Hinkson |first=Kamila |last2=Vecenie |first2=Sam |name-list-style=and |date=June 27, 2025 |title=Magic draft Jase Richardson, son of retired player Jason Richardson, at No. 25 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Richardson's father, [[Jason Richardson]], was a second-team All-American at Michigan State and a member of the [[1999–2000 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Spartans' 2000 national championship team]] and played in the [[National Basketball Association]] for 14 seasons. From age four through high school, Jase was coached by his mother, Jackie Paul-Richardson, who played basketball at the [[University of Colorado Colorado Springs|University of Colorado, Colorado Springs]]. Richardson's younger brother Jaxon is a consensus five-star basketball recruit in the class of 2026.{{cite web|url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2022/jun/17/former-nba-players-son-gets-offer/|title=THE RECRUITING GUY: Former NBA player's son gets offer|first=Richard|last=Davenport|work=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]|date=June 17, 2022|access-date=November 5, 2024}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{basketball stats}} *[https://msuspartans.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jase-richardson/15555 Michigan State Spartans bio] {{Orlando Magic current roster}} {{2025 NBA draft}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Richardson, Jase}} [[Category:2005 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Berkeley, California]] [[Category:Basketball players from Denver]] [[Category:Michigan State Spartans men's basketball players]] [[Category:Orlando Magic draft picks]] [[Category:Orlando Magic players]] [[Category:Osceola Magic players]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[Category:Shooting guards]]
